The Police Inspector of Yeshwanthapura Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act 2.
Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Manasa and the accused was solemnized on 21-06-2021 as per Hindu customs and rites.
At that time accused demanded and received Rs.2 lakhs in cash, one gold chain, one bracelet and suite clothes as dowry from CW2 and CW3.

After the marriage, CW1 was residing at house No.17, 1st Floor, 11th Cross, S.B.M. Colony, Brundavan Nagar,
Mathikere, Bengaluru with accused wherein the accused was subjected the CW1 to mental and physical cruelty for fetching additional dowry amount and demanded her salary to pay his debt,
house rent.

Further, on 17-12-2021 at around 11 pm, the accused picked up quarrel with CW1 for more dowry, when CW2 and CW3 questioned, accused told give the property in his name, otherwise he would marry someone else and abused them with filthiest language and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty.
First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1, the Sri Vinod Rathod, CW10/PSI of Yeshwanthpura Police Station registered Crime No.03/2022 against the accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) read with Sec.34 IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and drawn spot mahazar as per Ex.P2 on 15- 03-2022.

After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A) of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, has been framed,
read over and explained to the accused persons in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 11 witnesses and examined 3 witnesses and exhibited 5 documents.

The learned Senior APP prayed for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served as PW1 and the accused have compromised the matrimonial differences in M.C.
No.413/2025 and hence the examination of CW4 to CW11 was dispensed with by the order dated 25-04- 2025.

10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused found from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

2. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage, CW1 started residing at house No.17, 1st Floor, 11th Cross, S.B.M. 13. The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1& 2: In the Negative Point No.3 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1 & 2: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the KABC030016462023 CC No.1022/2023 prosecution has examined one witness,
which is as follows:
i. CW1 by name Smt. Manasa.K.N., being informant examined as PW1 and identified her signatures on Ex.P1 (Complaint) and Ex.P2(Spot Mahazar) as Ex.P1(a) and 2(a)
and deposed that when she went to the police station for sorting out the minor differences of opinion amongst her and the accused, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 and further stated that she did not lodge complaint against accused and no mahazar was conducted in her presence.
In this regard, the learned Sr.APP cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.

Her denial statement given before the police is marked as per Ex.P3.
ii.

CW3 by name Smt. Vimala and CW2 Sri Nagaraju the parents of CW1 examined as PW2 and PW3 respectively, pleaded ignorance about the prosecution case and deposed that they have not given any statement before the police in respect of alleged incident.

In this regard, the learned Sr.APP cross examined these witnesses by treating them as KABC030016462023 CC No.1022/2023 hostile witnesses but no favorable answers have been elicited from them to support the prosecution case.

sentences.text: On perusal of aforesaid recitation, it is clear that the disputes between the accused No.1 and CW1 (informant) have been settled wherein she received Rs.3 lakhs from accused as permanent alimony.

16. This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana and anr in the case of AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then KABC030016462023 CC No.1022/2023 in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
and in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat), wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances,
KABC030016462023 CC No.1022/2023 under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused No.1 have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498(A) of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.
17. In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464

sentences.text: wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".

Under these circumstances, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.
Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the ingredients for offences Under Section 498(A)

ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A) of KABC030016462023 CC No.1022/2023 Indian Penal Code and Sec.3,
